hints.content: To find the image of $\triangle ABC$ under the dilation, we can dilate all of $\triangle ABC$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD A$ is $1$ unit to the left of $P$ and $2$ units up, so its image is $\goldD3\cdot1=3$ units to the left and $\goldD3\cdot 2=6$ units up from $P$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Point B is two units to the left of point P and one unit down, Point C is two units right from point P, and Point A is one unit left of point P and two units up. There is a dashed line to highlight horizontally the three units left and vertically six units up from point P. There is also a dashed line to highlight horizontally one unit to the left and vertically two units up from point P.  There is another plotted point that is three units left and six units up from Point P.

hints.content:
Let's do the same thing with the remaining vertices.

Since our scale factor is $\goldD 3$, every side length in $\triangle A'B'C'$ will be $3$ times the length of the corresponding side in $\triangle ABC$.

Connecting the vertices of the image, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Point B is three units to the left of point P and three units up, Point C is two units down from point P, and Point A is three units right of point P and two units up. There is another triangle graphed that is triangle A B C with a scale factor of two from point P. The new triangle the Point B prime is six units to the left of point P and six units up, Point C prime is four units down from point P, and Point A prime is six units right of point P and four units up. The distance between C prime and B prime is approximately eleven point seven units. The distance between C prime and A prime is ten units. The distance between A prime and B prime is twelve point two units

question.content:
